newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers soft, Mideast seen falling further.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers soft, Mideast seen falling further.

text.p: The clean products tanker market was quiet and soft this week with little hope that it will pick up soon, brokers said on Friday. "Prospects are looking very gloomy for owners with overage tonnage in the Middle East. Modern tonnage under 15 years of age have less difficulty fixing, although rate levels are still very weak," said brokers E.A. Gibson in their weekly tanker report.
Referring to long-range Mideast/Japan voyages, they said: "Owners with tonnage open within the next two weeks will probably have to give discounts to get fixed."

Brokers put 55,000 tonnes to Japan currently at W175, unchanged from last week, while 30,000 tonnes Mideast/India was at about W170/175. However, nothing had been confirmed done to India sector this week, Gibson said.

The Med market was fairly strong, however. Gibson said there was a shortage of oil company-suitable jet and naphtha vessels, which kept cross-Med rates steady at W230 for 27,500 tonne stems, and there had also been some interest in fixing vessels from the Med to Asia, with about $1.25 million paid to Singapore.
The Caribbean market was dull, with around W255 paid to USAC. "It seems that there is little prospect of a return to healthier rate levels next week," Gibson said.
